## Statute
§152(c)(1) - Qualifying child requires meeting all four conditions: (A) relationship, (B) residence, (C) age, (E) no joint return
§152(c)(2)(A) - Relationship: child of the taxpayer
§152(c)(1)(B) - Residence: same principal place of abode for more than one-half of taxable year
§152(c)(3) - Age requirements: younger than taxpayer and less than 25 years old at end of taxable year
§152(c)(1)(E) - No joint return filed with spouse for the taxable year

## Reasoning
Under §152(c)(1), a qualifying child must meet ALL four requirements:

1. Relationship (§152(c)(2)(A)): Bob is Alice's son - SATISFIED

2. Residence (§152(c)(1)(B)): Alice and Bob lived together from January 1 through November 3, 2019 (more than half the year) - SATISFIED

3. Age (§152(c)(3)): Facts state Bob satisfied 152(c)(3) for 2015-2020 - SATISFIED

4. No Joint Return (§152(c)(1)(E)): The facts state Bob married Charlie on October 23rd, 2018, so Bob was married throughout 2019. However, the facts ONLY state that 'Bob satisfied section 152(c)(2) and 152(c)(3)' - they do NOT state that Bob satisfied all of 152(c)(1), and they do NOT explicitly state that Bob did not file a joint return with Charlie for 2019.

The claim states 'Under section 152(c)(1), Bob is a qualifying child of Alice for the year 2019.' This claim requires all four conditions to be met. Since the facts do NOT confirm that Bob did not file a joint return for 2019, we cannot conclude that all four conditions are satisfied.

The claim asserts something that the facts do not fully support - the joint return requirement is not addressed in the facts. Therefore, the claim is a CONTRADICTION because the facts do not establish that Bob is a qualifying child (all four conditions must be met, but one condition is not confirmed).

## Answer
Answer: Contradiction
